record.paper_title: Recent progress and open problems in the Bergman space
record.original_question: Let omega be a continuous nonnegative function on D such that omega(z) <= C(1 - |z|^2) for some positive constant C and omega is super-biharmonic, Delta^2 omega >= 0 in D. Are analytic polynomials dense in the weighted Bergman space L^2_a(D,omega) consisting of analytic functions f on D with integral_D |f(z)|^2 omega(z) dS(z) finite?

evidence.quote: PROBLEM 7 Suppose omega is a continuous function on D
Problem 7 as stated above has an affirmative answer

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{D} = \{z \in \mathbb{C} : |z| < 1\}$ denote the open unit disk and let $dS$ denote area measure on $\mathbb{D}$. Suppose $\omega : \mathbb{D} \to [0,\infty)$ is a continuous function satisfying:

(i) $\omega(z) \le C(1 - |z|^2)$ for all $z \in \mathbb{D}$ and some constant $C > 0$;

(ii) $\omega$ is super-biharmonic in $\mathbb{D}$, that is, $\Delta^2 \omega \ge 0$ in the sense of distributions on $\mathbb{D}$, where $\Delta$ is the Laplacian.

Define the weighted Bergman space
$$L^2_a(\mathbb{D}, \omega) = \Big\{ f : \mathbb{D} \to \mathbb{C} \text{ analytic} : \|f\|^2 := \int_{\mathbb{D}} |f(z)|^2 \omega(z)\, dS(z) < \infty \Big\}.$$

Determine whether the set of analytic polynomials is dense in $L^2_a(\mathbb{D}, \omega)$.
artifact.status_search_result: The density of analytic polynomials in weighted Bergman spaces with super-biharmonic, area-integrable weights has been established affirmatively (work by Abkar, Borichev, Hedenmalm and others on super-biharmonic weights), confirming polynomials are dense in such spaces.

status_evidence.title: Hedenmalm's work on super-biharmonic weights
status_evidence.snippet: Problem 7 as stated above has an affirmative answer.
status_evidence.claim: The density problem for polynomials in L^2_a(D,omega) with super-biharmonic weight has an affirmative answer.
